# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `go generate ./docs` from `siphon help --json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

`siphon` has two modes:

- **Client mode** talks to a running Siphon over its API, from any machine.
  Log in once with `siphon login <url>`, or set `SIPHON_URL` and
  `SIPHON_TOKEN_FILE`.
- **Local mode** works on the config file and the database directly
  (`serve`, `validate`, …). Any command given `-config` is local.

An AI assistant can read all of this as JSON: `siphon help --json`. It
should also read `siphon guide`.

## Flags for every client command

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--insecure-http` | `false` | allow http:// to a non-loopback host (default: SIPHON_INSECURE_HTTP=1; the token is then sent in clear text) |
| `-o` | `text` | output format: text or json |
| `--quiet` | `false` | print only data and errors, no progress messages |
| `--token-file` |  | file holding the API token (default: SIPHON_TOKEN_FILE, SIPHON_TOKEN, then client.yaml) |
| `--url` |  | siphon URL (default: the saved login, else SIPHON_URL; needs -token-file or SIPHON_TOKEN* unless it is the saved login's) |

Kinds for `get`: `sources`, `rules`, `agents`, `routines`, `credentials`, `jobs`, `approvals`, `audit`, `connections`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | error |
| 2 | usage |
| 3 | validation failed |
| 4 | not found |
| 5 | conflict (stale edit) |

With `-o json`, errors on stderr are `{"error": "…", "errors": […], "hint": "…"}`.

## Client commands

### siphon login

Save the server URL (default SIPHON_URL) and API token (token from a no-echo prompt, or stdin).

```sh
siphon login [url]
```

Example:

```sh
siphon login http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

### siphon logout

Forget the saved login.

```sh
siphon logout
```

Example:

```sh
siphon logout
```

### siphon status

Sources, rules, pending approvals and recent jobs at a glance.

```sh
siphon status
```

Example:

```sh
siphon status -o json
```

### siphon get

List or show config items (sources rules agents routines credentials) or jobs, approvals, audit, connections.

```sh
siphon get <kind> [name]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--event` |  | audit: only this event |
| `--limit` | `0` | jobs, audit: at most this many rows |
| `--rule` |  | audit: only this rule's rows |
| `--since` |  | audit: since a time (RFC 3339) or how long ago (1h) |
| `--state` |  | jobs: only this state |

Example:

```sh
siphon get rules disk-full
```

### siphon apply

Create or update items from a siphon.yaml-shaped file, all or nothing.

```sh
siphon apply -f <file|-> [--dry-run] [--secret k=@file|k=-] [--yes]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | `false` | check and show the diff, change nothing |
| `-f` |  | file to apply, or - for stdin |
| `--secret` |  | a secret value as <kind>/<name>.<field>=@file or =- (stdin); never a plain value |
| `--yes` | `false` | apply without asking |

Example:

```sh
siphon apply -f task.yaml --dry-run
```

### siphon edit

Edit one item in $EDITOR, with a stale-edit check.

```sh
siphon edit <kind> <name>
```

Example:

```sh
siphon edit rules disk-full
```

### siphon delete

Delete an item (a file item is hidden, a portal item removed).

```sh
siphon delete <kind> <name> [--dry-run]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | `false` | check and show the diff, change nothing |

Example:

```sh
siphon delete rules disk-full --dry-run
```

### siphon reset

Drop the portal's change to an item, back to siphon.yaml.

```sh
siphon reset <kind> <name> [--dry-run]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | `false` | check and show the diff, change nothing |

Example:

```sh
siphon reset rules disk-full
```

### siphon enable

Turn a rule on (runtime override).

```sh
siphon enable <rule>
```

Example:

```sh
siphon enable disk-full
```

### siphon disable

Turn a rule off (runtime override).

```sh
siphon disable <rule>
```

Example:

```sh
siphon disable disk-full
```

### siphon history

Config revisions, newest first; a revision number shows its diff.

```sh
siphon history [kind name | <rev>]
```

Example:

```sh
siphon history rules disk-full
```

### siphon restore

Put the config overlay back as it was at a revision.

```sh
siphon restore <rev> [--yes]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--yes` | `false` | restore without asking |

Example:

```sh
siphon restore 12 --yes
```

### siphon jobs

List jobs, or show one (with -config: the local `jobs ls`).

```sh
siphon jobs [ls|show <id>] [-state s]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | `0` | at most this many jobs |
| `--state` |  | only jobs in this state |

Example:

```sh
siphon jobs ls -state pending_approval
```

### siphon approve

Approve a pending job (with -config: local).

```sh
siphon approve <job id>
```

Example:

```sh
siphon approve 42
```

### siphon deny

Deny a pending job (with -config: local).

```sh
siphon deny <job id>
```

Example:

```sh
siphon deny 42
```

### siphon connect

Connect a service or model: flags for the fields, prompts for the rest, secrets only via - or @file.

```sh
siphon connect github|gitlab|aws|model|login [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--access-key-id` |  | aws role mode: base access key id as - or @file (with --secret-access-key) |
| `--api-key` |  | model, login: API key as - (stdin) or @file |
| `--base` |  | gitlab: base URL (default https://gitlab.com) |
| `--external-id` |  | aws role mode: external id |
| `--file` |  | login: a login file (kind login), or - for stdin |
| `--mode` |  | github: remote or local; aws: role or profile |
| `--name` |  | name of the source, credential or connection (default: the service or preset) |
| `--no-test` | `false` | skip the connection test |
| `--profile` |  | aws profile mode: profile name from server.aws.profiles |
| `--project` |  | gitlab: project path, like group/project |
| `--region` |  | aws: region |
| `--role-arn` |  | aws role mode: role ARN |
| `--secret-access-key` |  | aws role mode: base secret access key as - or @file |
| `--servers` |  | aws: servers to add, comma separated (cloudwatch, docs; default cloudwatch) |
| `--setup-token` |  | login claude: a setup token as - (stdin) or @file (kind token) |
| `--token` |  | github, gitlab: API token as - (stdin) or @file |
| `--url` |  | model: endpoint URL (default: the preset's) |
| `--webhook` | `false` | github, gitlab, aws: also create a webhook source (its secret is shown once) |

Example:

```sh
siphon connect github --name gh --token @token.txt --webhook
```

### siphon test

Dry-run a rule on an event, the last stored one, or (schedule rules) the event for a moment with --at; or check a service or model connection.

```sh
siphon test <rule> [event.json|-] [--last] [--at <time>] | test service|model <name>
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--at` |  | schedule rules: test the event for this moment, like "2026-03-02 06:00" (in the source's zone) |
| `--header` |  | an event header as name=value (repeatable) |
| `--last` | `false` | use the last event the source produced |

Example:

```sh
siphon test disk-full --last
```

### siphon why

Why a rule did or didn't fire: a checklist, the likely reason and what to run next.

```sh
siphon why <rule>
```

Example:

```sh
siphon why disk-full
```

### siphon new

Build a rule (and its source) with a wizard or flags, then dry-run, confirm and apply.

```sh
siphon new task [--name n --source s|--webhook w|--poll p --url u|--schedule at [--timezone Z] ...] [--print]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent` |  | run this existing agent |
| `--cmd` |  | run a command: argv as a JSON array, like '["notify","{{.event.msg}}"]' |
| `--cooldown` |  | minimum time between fires (required for agents) |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | check and show the diff, change nothing |
| `--every` | `5m` | poll interval, with --poll |
| `--id` |  | with --on each: the expression that identifies an event |
| `--name` |  | the rule's name |
| `--on` |  | each (once per --id) or edge (when the condition turns true; the default) |
| `--poll` |  | create an http polling source with this name (needs --url) |
| `--print` | `false` | only print the YAML, change nothing (pipe it to `siphon apply -f -`) |
| `--repeat` |  | with --on edge: fire again while true after this long |
| `--routine` |  | run this existing routine |
| `--schedule` |  | create a schedule source with this "at": a cron line, @daily, or "every 15m"; the source takes the task's name |
| `--source` |  | use this existing source |
| `--timezone` |  | with --schedule: an IANA zone like Europe/London (default: the server's local zone) |
| `--url` |  | the polled URL, with --poll |
| `--webhook` |  | create a webhook source with this name (a secret is generated and shown once) |
| `--when` |  | the condition, an expression over event, headers and item |
| `--yes` | `false` | apply without asking |

Example:

```sh
siphon new task --name alert --webhook alerts --when 'event.sev == "high"' --cmd '["notify"]' --print
```

### siphon template

List the ready-made task templates, or print one to pipe into `apply -f -`.

```sh
siphon template [name]  (alias: example)
```

Example:

```sh
siphon template github-pr-review > pr.yaml
```

### siphon explain

Every field of a config kind: type, required, default, allowed values.

```sh
siphon explain source|rule|agent|routine|credential
```

Example:

```sh
siphon explain rule -o json
```

### siphon inventory

Names of everything configured plus the operator's allowlists (never secrets).

```sh
siphon inventory
```

Example:

```sh
siphon inventory -o json
```

### siphon guide

Print the guide for LLM agents (docs/llm.md).

```sh
siphon guide
```

Example:

```sh
siphon guide
```

### siphon draft

Have a model connection draft an apply file from plain words; checked, never applied without --apply.

```sh
siphon draft "<text>" [--connection c] [--model m] [--apply] [--yes]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | `false` | apply the draft after showing the diff and asking |
| `--connection` |  | the model connection to ask (default: the first one) |
| `--model` |  | the model id (default: the connection's first listed model) |
| `--yes` | `false` | with --apply: don't ask |

Example:

```sh
siphon draft "tell me on ntfy when a deploy webhook reports failed"
```

### siphon mcp

Run an MCP server on stdio so an assistant can inspect and (with --allow-write) change this siphon.

```sh
siphon mcp [--allow-write] [--allow-secrets] [--allow-unapproved]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--allow-secrets` | `false` | with --allow-write: accept secret values through apply (they pass through the assistant's context) |
| `--allow-unapproved` | `false` | let apply turn an agent's approval off (default: refused) |
| `--allow-write` | `false` | let apply and delete really change things (default: they only dry-run) |

Example:

```sh
claude mcp add siphon -- siphon mcp
```

### siphon help

Usage; --json is the machine-readable command list.

```sh
siphon help [command] [--json]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | `false` | print the command list as JSON |

Example:

```sh
siphon help --json
```

## Local commands

### siphon validate

Check the config (file + portal edits; -file-only: file alone; -v: print egress allowlists).

```sh
siphon validate [-config f] [-v] [-file-only]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |
| `-v` | `false` | print egress allowlists |
| `--file-only` | `false` | ignore portal edits |

Example:

```sh
siphon validate -config siphon.yaml
```

### siphon config export

Print the effective YAML (file + portal edits).

```sh
siphon config export [-config f]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |

Example:

```sh
siphon config export -config siphon.yaml
```

### siphon rules test

Dry-run a rule against a saved event (JSON file).

```sh
siphon rules test [-config f] <rule> <event>
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |

Example:

```sh
siphon rules test -config siphon.yaml disk-full event.json
```

### siphon run-once

Poll every source once and run matching actions.

```sh
siphon run-once [-config f]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |

Example:

```sh
siphon run-once -config siphon.yaml
```

### siphon serve

Run the daemon.

```sh
siphon serve [-config f]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |

Example:

```sh
siphon serve -config siphon.yaml
```

### siphon credentials import

Store a login read from stdin.

```sh
siphon credentials import [-config f] [-token-stdin] <name>
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |
| `--token-stdin` | `false` | the input is a setup token, not a login file |

Example:

```sh
siphon credentials import -config siphon.yaml -token-stdin claude-main
```

### siphon credentials ls

List stored logins (no secrets).

```sh
siphon credentials ls [-config f]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | `siphon.yaml` | config file (runs the command locally, without the API) |

Example:

```sh
siphon credentials ls -config siphon.yaml
```

### siphon schema

Print the JSON Schema for siphon.yaml.

```sh
siphon schema
```

Example:

```sh
siphon schema
```

### siphon version

Print the version.

```sh
siphon version
```

Example:

```sh
siphon version
```
